s1.syndrome_frame: Asymptomatic calcified mass on the maxilla with a hard, mineralized structure
salient_findings: Asymptomatic, calcified mass on the right anterior maxilla
Mucosal fenestration with a visible hard, mineralized structure
Discrete radiopaque lesion on periapical radiograph
key_facts: Mass located on the right anterior maxilla
Mass has been present for 18 months
Hard, mineralized structure approximately 1 cm in diameter
Discrete radiopaque lesion on periapical radiograph

shortlist.label: Maxillary exostosis
shortlist.why_kept: Initial diagnostic hypothesis based on clinical presentation

shortlist.label: Compound odontoma
shortlist.why_kept: Possible cause of a calcified mass with a hard, mineralized structure

shortlist.label: Complex odontoma
shortlist.why_kept: Similar to compound odontoma, could explain the radiopaque lesion

shortlist.label: Periapical cemental dysplasia
shortlist.why_kept: Could be a cause of the discrete radiopaque lesion on the periapical radiograph

shortlist.label: Benign fibro-osseous lesion
shortlist.why_kept: Broad category that includes several possible diagnoses, including cemento-ossifying fibroma

shortlist.label: Cemento-ossifying fibroma
shortlist.why_kept: Specific type of benign fibro-osseous lesion that could explain the clinical findings

shortlist.label: Osteoma
shortlist.why_kept: Possible cause of a calcified mass, although less common in the maxilla

shortlist.label: Periapical cementoma
shortlist.why_kept: Could be a cause of the discrete radiopaque lesion, although less likely given the location

raw.rationale: The presence of a calcified, asymptomatic mass on the right anterior maxilla with a mucosal fenestration and a hard, mineralized structure is consistent with maxillary exostosis, which is a benign bony growth that can occur on the maxilla.

rejected.label: Compound odontoma
rejected.why: Typically presents as a collection of small, tooth-like structures, which is not described in the vignette

rejected.label: Complex odontoma
rejected.why: Usually appears as a radiopaque mass with a mix of radiolucent and radiopaque areas, not matching the discrete radiopaque lesion described

rejected.label: Periapical cemental dysplasia
rejected.why: Typically associated with the apical region of a vital tooth, which is not indicated in the vignette

rejected.label: Benign fibro-osseous lesion
rejected.why: A broader category that includes several lesions, but the specific characteristics described point more directly to maxillary exostosis

rejected.label: Cemento-ossifying fibroma
rejected.why: Often presents with a mix of radiolucent and radiopaque areas and can be more aggressive, which does not match the asymptomatic and discrete nature of the lesion

rejected.label: Osteoma
rejected.why: While osteoma could be considered, maxillary exostosis is more specific to the maxilla and the described characteristics

rejected.label: Periapical cementoma
rejected.why: Usually associated with a vital tooth and has a different radiographic appearance, not matching the description provided
